verified_entries.one_line_claim: In a three-advocate pipeline (critical / balanced / charitable advocates scoring political statements, aggregated by a supervisor), assigned advocate roles are only 39-67% faithful and collapse when fact-checks or training priors are unambiguous ('Epistemic Role Override').
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Same architecture in miniature: two opposed advocates plus a neutral seat plus an aggregating supervisor; they operationalise role fidelity (RDI/EDD/DDI/ERS) as the degree to which an advocate's output follows its assigned stance rather than the item -- the same quantity as our role-lock. verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: We measure role-lock at scale (1,663 crowd-adjudicated disputes) and find it near-total (0.971) rather than 39-67%; we score the ADVOCATES' verdict accuracy (0.595 / 0.438) and the COLLECTIVE'S accuracy against ground truth, which they explicitly do not do; we run the stake-vs-direction ablation (role-lock 0.946 without stake); we quantify dissent as an error sensor and test external override versus internal feedback. verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Mixed. closest_single_work.why: It is the only work found that builds essentially our architecture -- opposed advocate roles (critical / charitable) plus a balanced seat plus an aggregating supervisor -- and then measures the quantity we call role-lock: how far an advocate's output is set by its assigned stance rather than by the item. Its answer is the opposite of ours in magnitude (39-67% role fidelity vs our 0.971) and it identifies the mechanism that breaks role dominance: when the item has an unambiguous factual floor, the model's prior overrides the role ('Epistemic Role Override'). It does not score the advocates' or the collective's verdicts against ground truth, does not ablate stake vs direction, and does not touch sycophancy -- which is exactly the territory our measurements occupy. kelkar2026devil is the closest for the 'persona as directional control on sycophancy' framing, but it steers a single model's activations and builds no collective.

Strand 3: Persona / role / activation st.gap_our_results_fill_or_contradict: Three gaps, one of them a contradiction. (1) Role dominance: the literature either shows persona is a weak control on judgement (hu2024persona <10% variance; Santurkar 2023 'misalignment persists after steering'; Liu 2024 9.7% less steerable to incongruous stances) or, in the one directly comparable advocate pipeline (dietrich2026roles), finds roles hold only 39-67% and fail whenever facts are unambiguous. Nobody has reported a near-total lock (0.971) with a stake-vs-direction ablation (0.946 without stake) showing the pinning force is the directional case-making assignment. Our result is consistent with Dietrich's mechanism rather than against it: role dominance is near-total precisely on contested moral disputes where there is no epistemic floor -- and that is the regime in which the advocate's verdict is least informative. (2) Cost alongside benefit: the persona-cost literature (gupta2024bias, kim2025persona, Zheng 2024) measures accuracy loss but never pairs it with a benefit, and the persona-benefit literature (kelkar2026devil, shah2026toonice, chen2025persona, rimsky2024caa) measures sycophancy reduction on a single model and reports accuracy as preserved. No work shows both at once on the same agents: control strength 0.971, individual accuracy 0.595 / 0.438 (one below chance), collective effective voter count of one, yet a structured dissent signal (4.56x error density, phi = -0.72 anti-correlation) worth +0.193 when routed to an external judge. Kelkar's accuracy-preservation result versus our accuracy-collapse is the sharpest contrast in the strand: milder vector-level steering keeps the agent informative; total prompt-level embodiment does not. (3) Where objectivity comes from: chan2023chateval and wang2024spp claim role diversity makes a collective better than one agent; our panel contradicts the mechanism (majority = neutral seat on 1,663/1,663; one call beats 17 by +0.069; feedback iteration nets +0.012, null). What survives is khan2024debating's allocation of labour and kim2025persona's remedy: role-pinned agents are uninformative as generators, and objectivity is recovered only by an external, decorrelated selector reading the disagreement. Framed for the thesis: (A) is confirmed more strongly than any prior measurement; (B) as 'the graph does the reconciling' is contradicted by our own data -- the graph does the flagging, and the reconciling is done from outside it.

closest_single_work.why: It runs the same three-way comparison we ran (debate / single advocate / judge answering alone) with LLM judges and LLM agents, and reaches the same shape of result: debate beats a single assigned advocate, but once the judge can see the item there is no information asymmetry and debate does not beat the judge alone; stronger debaters add only modestly. That is the published equivalent of our neutral seat (0.852) and one grok call (0.912) beating the 17-call deliberation (0.843). What it does not do: assign INTERESTS (a party the verdict counts against) rather than truth-indexed positions, measure whether the advocates' outputs carry any item information, measure the dissent structure as an error flag, or test routing flagged items to an external decorrelated judge. Its debaters always include one who holds the true answer by construction; ours do not, which is why our advocates come out item-blind and theirs do not.

STRAND 1: Debate and scalable oversight.gap_our_results_fill_or_contradict: Lead result for the related-work section: nobody in the debate / scalable-oversight lineage assigns OPPOSED INTERESTS at inference time and then asks the two questions we answered, namely whether the advocates' outputs carry any item information and whether their disagreement is diagnostic of error. The lineage (Michael 2023, Khan 2024, Kenton 2024) assigns truth-indexed positions, so one debater always holds the correct answer and the judge's job is to find it; that is why debater quality is a lever on truth in Khan 2024 and why our party-indexed advocates, neither of whom holds the answer, come out as near-constant functions of role (role-lock 0.971, accuracies 0.595 and 0.438). Our stake ablation (role-lock 0.946 without the stake) shows the pinning force is the directional case-making assignment itself, which no work here isolates. Irving 2018's own framing already puts the locus of truth in the judge, not the debaters, and our result is a strong-form instance of that: the 3-seat majority equals the neutral seat on 1,663/1,663 debates, so the effective voter count is one. Kenton 2024 supplies the mechanism (no information asymmetry, so debate does not beat the judge alone) and Smit 2024 and Wang 2024 give the same single-call-beats-collective pattern on reasoning tasks. What our results ADD: (1) the embodied dissent is a structured, anti-correlated error flag (phi = -0.72; 4.56x error density when 2+ seats object) and routing on it to a cross-vendor judge yields +0.193 on the flagged set, beating a graph-free self-disagreement sensor by +0.020; the closest precedent for interaction-as-error-detector is Cohen 2023 (cross-examination inconsistency), not any debate paper. (2) Feeding the dissent back into the same agents is null (+0.012), which is the empirical instance of Estornell 2024 and Zhu 2026's formal result that homogeneous-agent debate preserves expected correctness and converges to the majority. What our results CONTRADICT in the thesis: (B) as a claim that graph structure reconciles a community of embodied agents into objectivity is not supported on a fixed complete graph; Wu 2025 (structure marginal, capability dominates) and Jiang 2026 (cooperative resolution beats adversarial debate at ICML 2026) point the same way, and Wu 2026 obtains its topology gains only by learning the reference graph with RL rather than by opposed interests. The honest positioning: embodiment is a near-total control on the individual (thesis A holds, at least for grok), and the collective built from it is a sensor whose value is realised only by an external decorrelated node outside the graph. Sachdeva 2025/2026 is the only other multi-model debate on AITA blame and reports no accuracy against the crowd verdict, so our accuracy accounting is new for this task. verified_entries.title: Improving Multi-Agent Debate with Sparse Communication Topology
verified_entries.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, year, venue and abstract all confirmed on the ACL Anthology page
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Multi-agent debate over sparse communication graphs (each agent sees only some neighbours) matches or beats fully-connected debate on reasoning and factuality tasks at much lower cost, and the framework extends to multimodal reasoning and alignment-labeling tasks.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Treat the communication graph as the manipulated variable in a multi-agent debate, compare against the fully-connected baseline, and include a judgment-style (alignment labeling) task rather than only math.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Assign opposed first-person stakes (their agents are homogeneous, role-neutral samplers); measure truth-tracking on crowd-adjudicated moral disputes with per-seat calibration; compute the collective's effective voter count and show the 3-seat majority equals one seat on every debate; measure dissent as an error sensor; compare against a single-call baseline and a cross-vendor external judge.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports the premise of (B) that topology is a legitimate independent variable, but mildly undercuts (B) as stated: their topology effects are efficiency effects ('comparable or superior' at lower cost), the dependent variable is task accuracy, and they never test whether any topology makes the collective exceed its best member.

verified_entries.authors: Chen Qian, Zihao Xie, YiFei Wang, Wei Liu, Kunlun Zhu, Hanchen Xia, Yufan Dang, Zhuoyun Du, Weize Chen, Cheng Yang, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun
verified_entries.title: Scaling Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Collaboration
verified_entries.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2025
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, year confirmed on the ICLR 2025 proceedings page; abstract and arXiv comment 'Accepted to ICLR-2025' also confirmed on https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07155
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Organising agents on directed acyclic graphs (chain, star, tree, mesh, layered, random) into a MacNet scales to over a thousand agents; irregular topologies beat regular ones; performance follows a logistic 'collaborative scaling law' in agent count.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Topology is the independent variable; edges carry structured instructor/assistant reconciliation; they vary graph family and size systematically.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes as the control on individual bias; ground truth from crowd adjudication; per-seat accuracy decomposition; effective voter count; a direct test of whether the collective beats its best member and a single call (it does not); dissent routing to an external judge.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports (B) in spirit (graph shape matters, irregular > regular) but their dependent variable is quality score on generation tasks, not truth-tracking, and the logistic growth in N is not tested against a single best sample. Our N_eff = 1 result on an adjudication task contradicts the implied monotone benefit of adding wired agents.

verified_entries.authors: Mingchen Zhuge, Wenyi Wang, Louis Kirsch, Francesco Faccio, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Jürgen Schmidhuber
verified_entries.title: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
verified_entries.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024), PMLR 235:62743-62767
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, volume, year, pages confirmed on the PMLR page; abstract and ICML comment also confirmed on https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16823 (arXiv title 'Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs')
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Agents and swarms are computational graphs whose node prompts and edges (who talks to whom) can be automatically optimised; optimised edge structures improve on hand-designed ones and learn to disconnect adversarial agents.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Treat the inter-agent graph as the object that determines the collective's output and show that changing edges changes outcomes; include an adversarial (biased) node, a cousin of our stake-pinned advocate.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: We hold topology fixed and interrogate what the collective is doing (N_eff, per-seat information, dissent structure) instead of optimising it; stakes as control; ground truth from crowds; external override.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Neutral-to-supportive of the premise of (B) that edges matter. Notably their edge optimiser's fix for a bad agent is to isolate it, an external selection step, which is consistent with our finding that the useful graph operation is override/removal, not convergence. They optimise task reward, never objectivity, and never ask whether the optimum beats the best single node.

verified_entries.authors: Zijun Liu, Yanzhe Zhang, Peng Li, Yang Liu, Diyi Yang
verified_entries.title: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration
verified_entries.venue: COLM 2024 (venue stated in the arXiv comments field: 'Published in COLM2024'; OpenReview page blocked by a browser check this session)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, year (v1 Oct 2023, v2 Nov 2024) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; venue taken from the authors' arXiv comment field only
verified_entries.one_line_claim: DyLAN models collaboration as a temporal feed-forward network, selects a team via an 'Agent Importance Score', lets agents communicate in a dynamic structure, and early-stops on agreement; improves code, decision-making and reasoning tasks.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: A dynamic communication structure, an explicit per-agent importance score (the nearest thing in this literature to weighting members by contribution), and an agreement-based stopping rule.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Show that importance collapses to one seat (majority = neutral on 1,663/1,663); use disagreement as a positive signal rather than agreement as a stop; stakes; ground truth from crowds; single-call and external-judge comparators.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Neutral. Their importance score is used to prune a team, not to test whether the team is effectively larger than one; they report no truth-tracking dependent variable.

verified_entries.authors: Jintian Zhang, Xin Xu, Ningyu Zhang, Ruibo Liu, Bryan Hooi, Shumin Deng
verified_entries.title: Exploring Collaboration Mechanisms for LLM Agents: A Social Psychology View
verified_entries.venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), ACL 2024
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, year, venue and abstract confirmed on the ACL Anthology page
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Societies of LLM agents given a trait (easy-going vs overconfident) and a thinking pattern (debate vs reflection) show human-like conformity and consensus-reaching; some society configurations beat prior approaches at lower token cost.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Assign a disposition to each agent as a control on its behaviour (a cousin of our embodiment control), run multi-round societies, and measure conformity as an outcome on three benchmarks.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Our assigned property is an opposed interest, not a temperament; we quantify role-lock (0.971), compute N_eff, and find that opposed stakes produce anti-correlated dissent (phi = -0.72) rather than conformity; ground truth is crowd adjudication of moral disputes; we add an external cross-vendor override.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports (A): assigned traits measurably shift agent behaviour. Undercuts (B): conformity is the dominant dynamic they observe, i.e. the collective tends to collapse toward a single voice. Our stakes block conformity between advocates, but at the price of those seats carrying no item information.

verified_entries.authors: Junlin Wang, Jue Wang, Ben Athiwaratkun, Ce Zhang, James Zou
verified_entries.title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
verified_entries.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2025
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, year confirmed on the ICLR 2025 proceedings page; abstract confirmed on https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04692 (arXiv page itself states no venue)
verified_entries.one_line_claim: A layered topology in which every agent conditions on all previous-layer outputs and a final aggregator synthesises them lets open-source models beat GPT-4o on AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench and FLASK.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: A fixed DAG with a terminal aggregator node (analogue of our moderator/external judge) and heterogeneous models at different nodes.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes; ground truth; a test of whether the aggregator adds over the best proposer; dissent sensing; effective voter count.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Neutral on (B). Supports the value of cross-model heterogeneity at the aggregation node (our cross-vendor override), but the dependent variable is preference win-rate, not truth-tracking.

verified_entries.authors: Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Jingwei Zuo, Cheng Yang, Chenfei Yuan, Chi-Min Chan, Heyang Yu, Yaxi Lu, Yi-Hsin Hung, Chen Qian, Yujia Qin, Xin Cong, Ruobing Xie, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun, Jie Zhou
verified_entries.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
verified_entries.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2024
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, year confirmed on the ICLR 2024 proceedings page; abstract confirmed on https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10848 (arXiv page says 'Under review')
verified_entries.one_line_claim: A recruit/decide/act/evaluate framework with horizontal (all-to-all) or vertical (solver plus reviewers) decision structures; groups outperform a single agent and exhibit emergent social behaviours including conformity and destructive behaviour.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Compare two decision topologies and observe conformity as an emergent behaviour of the group.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Everything quantitative: role-lock, per-seat accuracy, N_eff, dissent structure, ground-truth comparison to a single call, external override.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Neutral. Qualitative reports of conformity foreshadow the collapse we measure, but there is no truth-tracking dependent variable and no test of topology against the best member.

verified_entries.authors: Xu Shen, Yixin Liu, Yiwei Dai, Yili Wang, Rui Miao, Yue Tan, Shirui Pan, Xin Wang
verified_entries.title: Understanding the Information Propagation Effects of Communication Topologies in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
verified_entries.venue: arXiv preprint (no venue stated on the abstract page)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (29 May 2025) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; no venue on page
verified_entries.one_line_claim: A causal analysis of how correct versus erroneous agent outputs propagate under topologies of varying sparsity finds moderately sparse graphs, which suppress error propagation while preserving beneficial diffusion, are typically optimal; EIB-Learner fuses dense and sparse connectivity.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Topology sparsity is the independent variable and the mechanism studied is propagation of error versus truth through the graph, the closest published treatment of 'the graph doing the reconciling'.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes as the source of bias; per-seat information content and N_eff; a test of whether any topology beats the best member; anti-correlated dissent as a sensor; external cross-vendor override on flagged items.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports the premise of (B) that graph structure governs whether errors or truth spread. But their conclusion, that the graph's useful job is to suppress propagation from bad nodes, aligns with our null on feeding dissent back to the same agents and with our finding that isolation/override, not convergence, is where the gain is.

verified_entries.authors: Chen Han, Jin Tan, Bohan Yu, Wenzhen Zheng, Xijin Tang
verified_entries.title: Conformity Dynamics in LLM Multi-Agent Systems: The Roles of Topology and Self-Social Weighting
verified_entries.venue: arXiv preprint (comments field: 'Under Review')
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (9 Jan 2026) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; no venue
verified_entries.one_line_claim: On a misinformation-detection task, network topology (centralized aggregation vs distributed consensus) and a confidence-normalised self-vs-social weight govern collective judgment: centralized is fast but hostage to hub competence and shows same-model alignment bias; distributed is more robust; more connectivity speeds convergence but raises 'wrong-but-sure cascades'.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: This is the direct answer to the strand's key question: topology as independent variable and truth-tracking (misinformation detection) as dependent variable, with a tunable self-reliance versus social-influence weight analogous to our stake.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Our control is an opposed first-person stake rather than a scalar self/social weight; ground truth is crowd adjudication of moral disputes; we compute N_eff and per-seat accuracy; we compare to a single call and to a cross-vendor judge; we route on dissent.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Partially supports (B): topology changes truth-tracking. But 'wrong-but-sure cascades' growing with connectivity and 'same-model alignment bias' undercut the idea that denser reconciliation yields objectivity, consistent with our null on internal steering.

verified_entries.authors: Blaž Bertalanič, Carolina Fortuna
verified_entries.title: The Ringelmann Effect in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Scaling Law for Effective Team Size
verified_entries.venue: arXiv preprint (comments: '41 pages, 9 figures, 20 tables'; no venue stated)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (31 May 2026) and full abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; no venue
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Derives a two-parameter law R(N) = N_eff/N = 1/(1 + c(N-1)N^-beta) whose regime exponent classifies any configuration as hard-ceiling, sublinear or linear; across 44 cells (peer debate, self-correction, noise placebo, self-consistency, heterogeneous teams, sparse communication, 7B-32B open models plus Gemini) the form fits at R^2 > 0.99; thirty dense debating agents give no more answer diversity than one on MMLU-Hard; a noise placebo tracks self-correction so the 'debate' gain is re-evaluation not peer content; only architectural diversity (heterogeneous teams) lowers c and escapes the hard ceiling, communication-mode interventions do not.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Define exactly our 'effective voter count' as a scalar order parameter (N_eff/N), include sparse communication and debate as conditions and find they do not change the regime, show that peer exchange is a re-sample rather than new evidence, and find that heterogeneity is the only escape from the ceiling (our cross-vendor judge).
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Use assigned stakes/embodiment as the control and show it maximises disagreement without raising N_eff; work on crowd-adjudicated moral disputes rather than math/MMLU; measure structured anti-correlated dissent as an error sensor and a routing intervention with a measured gain; ablate directional assignment from stake.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Strongly undercuts (B) as a graph theory of objectivity and strongly supports our measured shape: for homogeneous teams N_eff sits at a hard ceiling regardless of communication topology, and only decorrelated members raise it. Caveat: arXiv-only, no peer-reviewed venue.

verified_entries.authors: Hyeong Kyu Choi, Xiaojin Zhu, Sharon Li
verified_entries.title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
verified_entries.venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Spotlight)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, dates and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page (comments: 'NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight'); title, authors, 'NeurIPS 2025' and 'Spotlight Poster' also confirmed on https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/poster/116557
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Decomposing MAD into majority voting plus inter-agent debate across seven benchmarks, majority voting accounts for most of the gain; debate is proven to induce a martingale over belief trajectories, so debate alone does not change expected correctness; only interventions that bias the update toward correction help.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Test whether the exchange between agents adds anything beyond sampling, and prove formally that it is a re-sample of the same expectation; show that an external corrective bias is what moves accuracy.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes; ground truth from crowds; the stronger result that the majority is literally one seat; dissent as a structured sensor; cross-vendor override measured on the flagged subset.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B): reconciliation by exchange is expectation-preserving. Directly supports our 'a re-sample of the same posterior, not new evidence' reading and our external-override result.

verified_entries.authors: Andrew Estornell, Yang Liu
verified_entries.title: Multi-LLM Debate: Framework, Principals, and Interventions
verified_entries.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024), Main Conference Track
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, year and abstract confirmed on the NeurIPS proceedings page
verified_entries.one_line_claim: A mathematical framework for debate shows that similar model capabilities or similar responses produce static dynamics that simply converge to the majority opinion, and when that majority encodes a shared training-data misconception debate converges to the wrong answer; three interventions (diversity-pruning, quality-pruning, misconception-refutation) improve debate.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Theory of when a wired collective converges to its (possibly wrong) majority, and interventions that inject decorrelation from outside the loop.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Empirical measurement with stakes; show the majority is one seat; measure dissent structure; test an external cross-vendor override rather than pruning.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B) for agents drawn from the same model; supports the decorrelation route to objectivity.

verified_entries.authors: Hangfan Zhang, Zhiyao Cui, Jianhao Chen, Xinrun Wang, Qiaosheng Zhang, Zhen Wang, Dinghao Wu, Shuyue Hu
verified_entries.title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
verified_entries.venue: arXiv position paper (page comment: 'This position paper takes a critical view of the status quo of MAD research'; no venue stated on the page; OpenReview blocked this session)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (12 Feb 2025) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; venue not confirmed
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Across 5 MAD methods, 9 benchmarks and 4 base models, MAD often fails to beat Chain-of-Thought and Self-Consistency while consuming far more compute; model heterogeneity (Heter-MAD) consistently improves MAD frameworks.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Compare multi-agent collectives to a single-call baseline at matched cost and find the collective loses; identify cross-model heterogeneity as the fix.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes; crowd ground truth on moral disputes; N_eff; dissent as a sensor; targeted routing of the flagged 20% to a different vendor rather than blanket heterogeneity.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B) as a generator (matches our one-call-beats-17 result) and supports our cross-vendor override.

verified_entries.authors: Andries Petrus Smit, Nathan Grinsztajn, Paul Duckworth, Thomas D. Barrett, Arnu Pretorius
verified_entries.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
verified_entries.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024), PMLR 235:45883-45905
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, volume, year, pages confirmed on the PMLR page; abstract confirmed on https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17371
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Benchmarking debate and prompting strategies for truthfulness, MAD systems in their current form do not reliably outperform self-consistency or ensembling over reasoning paths; they are hyperparameter-sensitive, and tuning agent agreement levels can lift them above non-debate protocols.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Compare debate collectives against single-model ensembles on truthfulness, and treat agent agreement level as a tunable dial (a cousin of our stake ablation).
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes as the dial; ground truth from crowds; N_eff; dissent as a sensor; external override.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B) as a generator: debate does not reliably beat resampling the same model.

verified_entries.authors: Qineng Wang, Zihao Wang, Ying Su, Hanghang Tong, Yangqiu Song
verified_entries.title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
verified_entries.venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), ACL 2024
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, year, venue and abstract confirmed on the ACL Anthology page
verified_entries.one_line_claim: A single agent with a strong prompt reaches almost the same best performance as the best multi-agent discussion approach across reasoning tasks and backbones; discussion only helps when there is no demonstration in the prompt.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: The same single-call versus discussion comparison as our 'one grok call (0.912) beats the 17-call deliberation (0.843)'.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes; crowd ground truth; N_eff; dissent as a sensor; external override.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B) as a generator; matches our single-call result.

verified_entries.authors: Blaž Bertalanič, Carolina Fortuna
verified_entries.title: The Cost of Consensus: Isolated Self-Correction Prevails Over Unguided Homogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
verified_entries.venue: arXiv preprint (comments field: '19 pages, ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems'; not independently confirmed on a proceedings page)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (29 Apr 2026) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; venue from comments field only
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Ten homogeneous 7-8B agents over three rounds on GSM-Hard and MMLU-Hard fail via sycophantic conformity (modal adoption up to 85.5%), contextual fragility (up to 70% of correct answers destabilised by peers) and consensus collapse (oracle gap up to 32.3 pp); density ablation over K in {2,4,9} shows conformity saturates at K=2; isolated self-correction gives equal or better accuracy at 2.1-3.4x fewer tokens.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Communication density (a topology parameter) as an ablated independent variable with truth as dependent variable; an oracle-gap measurement (correct answer present but discarded) that parallels our cross-validated oracle over everything the panel emits; a noise placebo isolating re-evaluation from peer content.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Stakes that prevent conformity between advocates (phi = -0.72); crowd-adjudicated moral disputes; a frontier model; N_eff; a routing gain measured on the flagged subset.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B) and supports our shape (internal correction null; consensus discards information). One contrast worth stating: their oracle gap is positive (a correct answer exists somewhere in the pool) whereas our oracle over everything the panel emits (0.831) is worse than the neutral seat alone (0.852), i.e. our stake-pinned seats do not even contribute a hidden correct answer.

verified_entries.authors: Elliot Myunghoon Kim, Avi Garg, Kenny Peng, Nikhil Garg
verified_entries.title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
verified_entries.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2025), PMLR 267:30038-30066
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, venue, volume, year, pages confirmed on the PMLR page; abstract and 'Accepted to ICML 2025' confirmed on https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07962
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Across 350+ LLMs, errors are substantially correlated (on one leaderboard models agree 60% of the time when both err); larger and more accurate models have highly correlated errors even across providers and architectures, with consequences for LLM-as-judge and hiring.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Measure the independence assumption that any Condorcet-style graph-of-voters theory of objectivity requires, and find it violated.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Attempt decorrelation within one model via stakes (finding it decorrelates verdicts but not information), and measure the residual gain from a different vendor on flagged items.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Undercuts (B) as normally conceived: independent voters cannot be manufactured by wiring copies of one model. Also tempers our cross-vendor override: it works (+0.193 on flagged) but its ceiling is bounded by cross-provider error correlation.

verified_entries.authors: Chuan He, Zebin Chen, Zhengyi Yang, Shaobo Qiao, Mingchen Ju, Jiate Liu, Dong Wen, Guanfeng Liu
verified_entries.title: Minority Sentinel: When to Overturn Majority Voting in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
verified_entries.venue: AgentSearch Workshop at SIGIR 2026 (per the arXiv comments field; not independently confirmed on a proceedings page)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (28 Jun 2026) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; venue from comments field only
verified_entries.one_line_claim: With three heterogeneous debaters on six benchmarks, about one in four divergent cases has the minority correct ('Minority Truth'); a non-LLM meta-classifier over debate-log fingerprints decides when to overturn the majority (flip precision 81.2%, positive net gain on all datasets and seeds), while an LLM-as-judge baseline yields negative net gain despite higher recall.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Treat disagreement among seats as the trigger for an external decision, exactly the architecture of our dissent-routing, and measure that flip safety, not recovery volume, determines value.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Generate the disagreement from embodied opposed stakes and show it is structured (phi = -0.72, exactly one objector on 80% of debates); crowd ground truth on moral disputes; compare the embodied flag against a graph-free sample-disagreement flag; use a cross-vendor LLM judge and find it positive on flagged items.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports the error-sensor half of our shape. Their negative LLM-as-judge result is in tension with our positive cross-vendor override and must be reported; the reconciling hypothesis is that their judge shares the debaters' blind spots whereas ours is a different vendor (consistent with Kim et al. 2025).

verified_entries.authors: Cristiano De Nobili
verified_entries.title: Collective Alignment in LLM Multi-Agent Systems: Disentangling Bias from Cooperation via Statistical Physics
verified_entries.venue: arXiv preprint (comments: '10 pages, 7 figures'; no venue stated)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, author, submission date (11 May 2026) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; no venue
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Identical LLM agents on an L x L lattice holding yes/no states updated from four neighbours show temperature-driven order-disorder crossovers; extracting an effective coupling (social conformity) and field (intrinsic bias) shows collective alignment is dominated by intrinsic bias (h >> J), producing field-driven crossovers rather than genuine phase transitions.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: A literal order-parameter treatment (magnetisation, susceptibility) of an LLM collective on a fixed topology that decomposes the group outcome into neighbour coupling versus intrinsic bias.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Treat the 'field' as a control input (the assigned stake) and show it dominates (role-lock 0.971); measure truth rather than alignment; use a decision task with ground truth.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports (A): the intrinsic/assigned bias term dominates. Undercuts (B): neighbour coupling (the graph) is the weak term, so no topology-driven transition to objectivity should be expected from wiring alone.

verified_entries.authors: Zhiyuan Weng, Guikun Chen, Wenguan Wang
verified_entries.title: Do as We Do, Not as You Think: the Conformity of Large Language Models
verified_entries.venue: ICLR 2025 (Oral) per the arXiv comments field (OpenReview blocked this session)
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, submission date (23 Jan 2025) and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; venue from comments field only
verified_entries.one_line_claim: BenchForm, a benchmark of reasoning tasks under five interaction protocols, measures conformity rate and independence rate of LLMs in multi-agent settings, studies interaction timing and group size as drivers, and proposes enhanced personas and reflection as mitigations.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: Measure conformity as a function of interaction protocol and group size (topology-adjacent variables) and test persona assignment as a mitigation, a cousin of our embodiment control.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: Opposed stakes rather than personas; crowd ground truth on moral disputes; N_eff; dissent as a sensor; external override.
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports (A) in that persona assignment moves conformity; undercuts (B) in that conformity is the default dynamic of a wired collective.

verified_entries.authors: Tian Liang, Zhiwei He, Wenxiang Jiao, Xing Wang, Yan Wang, Rui Wang, Yujiu Yang, Shuming Shi, Zhaopeng Tu
verified_entries.title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate

closest_single_work.why: It is the only work found that defines the exact quantity the programme measured -- an effective voter count N_eff as a scalar order parameter of the collective -- fits it across debate, self-correction, placebo, sparse communication and heterogeneous conditions, and reaches the same conclusion: homogeneous collectives sit at a hard ceiling that no communication-mode intervention lifts, the apparent 'debate gain' is re-evaluation rather than peer content, and only decorrelated (architecturally different) members escape the ceiling. On the narrower question of topology as independent variable with truth-tracking as dependent variable, Han et al. 2026 (han2026conformity) is the closest, and Shen et al. 2025 (shen2025propagation) is the closest on error-propagation mechanics; but neither has an order parameter or tests the collective against its best member. Caveat for citation: Bertalanic and Fortuna 2026 is an arXiv preprint with no stated venue, and its evidence is on math/MMLU with 7B-32B open models plus one Gemini check, not on adjudicated disputes with a frontier reasoning model.

Strand 2: Communication topology of LLM.gap_our_results_fill_or_contradict: Where the literature stands: this strand treats the communication graph as an independent variable (li2024sparse, qian2025macnet, zhuge2024gptswarm, liu2024dylan, shen2025propagation, han2026conformity), but the dependent variable is almost always task accuracy or cost, and the comparison is almost always against a fully-connected graph or a hand-designed pipeline, never against the collective's own best member or a single call. Only han2026conformity puts truth-tracking (misinformation detection) on the y-axis against topology, and only bertalanic2026ringelmann and denobili2026collective offer a scalar order parameter (N_eff/N with regime exponent beta; effective field h versus coupling J). Independently, a second line (smit2024mad, wang2024rethinking, estornell2024multillm, zhang2025stopovervaluing, choi2025debateorvote, bertalanic2026costconsensus, kim2025correlated) has converged on the answer to 'does the collective beat its best member': for agents drawn from one model, no -- exchange is a martingale (Choi), a noise placebo matches debate (Bertalanic), majority voting carries the gain, and only cross-model heterogeneity moves the ceiling. So the programme's 'effective voter count = 1' is not new in kind; it has been found by others, most sharply by bertalanic2026ringelmann ('thirty dense debating agents produce no more answer diversity than one'). What our results add that no entry in this strand has: (1) A different source of decorrelation. Every escape route in the literature is model heterogeneity, pruning, or a self/social weighting scalar. We decorrelate by assigning opposed first-person stakes to copies of one model, and we measure the outcome precisely: it maximises disagreement (phi = -0.72, exactly one objector on 80% of debates) while leaving N_eff at 1 (majority = neutral on 1,663/1,663) and the stake-pinned seats below chance on item content. That is a new and somewhat contradicting point on the diversity-versus-accuracy curve: role diversity manufactures disagreement about the verdict without manufacturing information about the item, so it does not lower the Ringelmann constant c the way architectural diversity does. The ablation showing directional assignment alone (no stake) keeps role-lock at 0.946 locates the pinning force more precisely than any persona/trait manipulation in zhang2024socialpsych or weng2025conformity. (2) Dissent as a calibrated error sensor with a measured routing gain. he2026minoritysentinel and choi2025debateorvote both argue that disagreement should trigger an external correction, and Shen and Han show graphs can suppress or amplify error propagation; none reports the 4.56x error density under 2+ objections, the comparison of an embodied dissent flag against a graph-free sample-disagreement flag (+0.020), or the routing gain on the flagged subset (+0.193). Our positive cross-vendor-judge result is in direct tension with Minority Sentinel's negative LLM-as-judge result and should be presented as such, with kim2025correlated's provider-correlation finding as the candidate explanation. (3) The internal-steering null with a stake-maximised collective. Choi's martingale and Bertalanic's placebo show that feedback among same-model agents is expectation-preserving; we show it stays null (+0.012) even when the seats are wired to disagree as hard as stakes can make them, on a task with no formal ground truth (crowd-adjudicated moral disputes) and with a frontier reasoning model rather than 7B-32B open models. (4) Domain. Every order-parameter and collective-versus-best-member result above is on math, MMLU or code; ours is the first on crowd-adjudicated interpersonal disputes, where the case for a 'graph theory of objectivity' is strongest and where we still find the collective is a sensor, not a generator. Net: the honest framing for the paper is that the strand already contains the negative result on (B) for wired copies of one model; our contribution is showing that embodied stakes are a near-total control on the individual (A) that does not convert into a collective advantage (B), and that the only graph operation that yielded objectivity was an edge to a decorrelated external node, activated where the embodied seats disagreed."

verified_entries.title: Why do humans reason? Arguments for an argumentative theory
verified_entries.venue: Behavioral and Brain Sciences 34(2):57-74, doi:10.1017/S0140525X10000968
verified_entries.verified_fields: title, authors, year, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI, abstract (all confirmed on the Cambridge Core article page; abstract also cross-checked against the CUP-deposited Crossref record)
verified_entries.one_line_claim: Reasoning evolved to produce and evaluate arguments for persuasion, not to track truth individually; confirmation bias is what an argument-producer should show, and epistemic gains come from the exchange of arguments between people who disagree.
verified_entries.what_they_did_that_we_do: They make, at the level of theory and reinterpreted human data, exactly the two moves the thesis makes: (A) an individual reasoner is an advocate whose outputs are a function of the position it is defending ('skilled arguers are not after the truth but after arguments supporting their views'), and (B) truth-conducive outcomes are a property of the argumentative exchange, not of any individual. Our role-lock number (0.971; advocates are near-constant functions of role) is the LLM instantiation of their claim about producers.
verified_entries.what_we_do_that_they_do_not: They never build or measure a group; the group-correction half of the theory is an inference from human studies. We instantiate both halves with LLM agents and measure them separately: the producer half holds (role-lock), the exchange half does not (steering null +0.012; 3-seat majority equals the neutral seat on 1,663/1,663 debates; 17-call deliberation 0.843 < one call 0.912). We also add what their account has no slot for: an external, decorrelated judge that overrides the group where the group flags itself (+0.193 on the flagged 20%).
verified_entries.supports_or_undercuts_thesis: Supports (A) strongly and PREDICTS role-lock. On (B) it is undercut in our setting: the theory does not require a disinterested evaluator (evaluation is done by the same, epistemically vigilant receivers), but it does require that the exchange contain someone holding the right answer and the arguments for it. Our advocates hold no item information (accuracy 0.595 / 0.438), so the exchange has nothing to converge on beyond the neutral seat; the 'group corrects' prediction is not falsified so much as vacuously unmet, while the stronger generic claim that adding conflict improves outcomes is contradicted (adding two advocates made the aggregate worse than one call).

closest_single_work.why: Mercier & Sperber 2011 (with The Enigma of Reason as its book-length form) is the only work in the strand that states both halves of the thesis as one theory: individuals reason as advocates whose outputs track the position they defend (our role-lock, 0.971, is a near-perfect LLM instantiation of this), and epistemically good outcomes are produced by the exchange of arguments among people who disagree, not by any individual. It also answers the strand's key question directly: the theory does not require a disinterested evaluator, because the same reasoner is a lazy producer and a vigilant evaluator (Trouche et al. 2016). That is precisely the property our role-assigned agents lack. For the empirical shape of our negative result the closest work is Nemeth, Brown & Rogers 2001: role-played devil's advocacy does not clone authentic dissent and mainly provokes bolstering, which is the human precedent for steering failure.

Strand 5: The argumentative theory of re.gap_our_results_fill_or_contradict: The argumentative theory predicts two things and we confirm one and fail the other. (1) Confirmed: an agent given a side is a biased advocate whose output is a function of the side. We go further than the human literature by showing the pinning is total (0.3% vs 97.4% at-fault; role-lock 0.971) and that it is driven by the directional case-making instruction, not the stake (0.946 without stake), so 'interest' in the thesis's sense is doing almost nothing; the instruction to argue a direction is the control input. (2) Not confirmed: Mercier 2016's explicit prediction that 'the more debate and conflict between opinions there is, the more argument evaluation prevails over argument production, resulting in better outcomes'. Our added conflict made the aggregate worse than a single call (0.843 vs 0.912), the panel's majority was the neutral seat on 1,663/1,663 debates, and returning the dissent to the agents netted +0.012 (null). The literature itself supplies three reasons, each of which our design triggers: (a) Trouche et al. 2014 / Laughlin & Ellis: 'truth wins' needs a demonstrable answer and a member who holds it and argues for it; our advocate seats hold no item information (0.595 / 0.438) and AITA is a judgmental task; (b) Nemeth et al. 2001: contrived, role-played dissent does not reproduce the epistemic benefits of authentic dissent and tends to bolster rather than move positions; (c) Longino 2002: a community is objective only if criticism gets uptake, and our advocates are constructed not to take it up; a complete graph satisfies her venue norm and fails her uptake norm, which is the structural diagnosis of why the graph did not reconcile anything. Where our results extend rather than contradict the strand: the dissent channel is a genuine, structured error sensor (4.56x error density when 2+ seats object; objections anti-correlated at phi = -0.72; beats a graph-free self-disagreement sensor by +0.020), and the cure that works (+0.193 on flagged items) is routing that signal to an external, decorrelated arbiter. That matches the adversarial-collaboration protocol of Mellers, Hertwig & Kahneman 2001, which requires an arbiter and in which the advocates still did not converge on interpretation, and it matches a Popperian reading in which the adversarial community is a good falsifier and a poor generator. The honest framing for the paper: the thesis's part (A) is a stronger control than the human literature ever measured; part (B), reconciliation through graph structure, is contradicted for the complete-graph-plus-moderator design on both a judgmental (AITA) and an intellective (BrokenMath, -0.026) instrument, and the literature's own conditions for collective correction (informed disputants, demonstrable answers, uptake of criticism, an arbiter) name the ingredients the design lacked. The Schwenk 1990 meta-analytic result that devil's advocacy beats a lone expert is the specific prior our one-call-beats-panel result reverses in the LLM setting.

closest_single_work.why: It is the one theorem in this strand that literally states a graph-theoretic condition for a community to converge to truth, which is what 'a graph theory of objectivity where reconciliation is driven through graph structures' asks for. Its condition (the most influential agent's eigenvector weight must vanish) is the precise thing our measurements violate: the neutral seat has influence weight 1 (majority = neutral on 1,663/1,663; oracle over all panel output 0.831 < neutral alone 0.852). More importantly, the theorem's precondition fails before its condition does: Golub-Jackson agents each hold an independent unbiased noisy signal, whereas our embodied advocates hold a role-determined constant (0.3% vs 97.4% at-fault, accuracies 0.595 and 0.438). With two constant opposed nodes, any wiring that reduces the neutral's influence, which is what the theorem would prescribe, moves the consensus toward a role-determined constant, not toward truth. Bahrami et al. 2010 is the closest empirical match to the headline number (communicating with much weaker partners makes the group worse than its best member), and Nitzan-Paroush/Shapley-Grofman is the closest formal match to Lambda = 1 (log-odds weights 1.75 vs 0.385 and -0.249 make the neutral seat the optimal decision rule), but Golub-Jackson is the work that frames the thesis itself.

Strand 4: Formal social epistemology and.gap_our_results_fill_or_contradict: Which formal results directly predict the measurements, stated precisely. (1) Dictatorship, Lambda = 1: Nitzan-Paroush 1982 and Shapley-Grofman 1984 say the accuracy-optimal rule over independent binary voters is weighted majority with w_i = ln(p_i/(1-p_i)). With the measured seat accuracies this gives w_neutral = 1.75, w_writer = 0.385, w_counterparty = -0.249 (below chance, vote should be inverted); since 0.385 + 0.249 < 1.75 the optimal rule is the neutral seat alone. So the observed majority = neutral on every debate, and the failure of a cross-validated oracle over all panel emissions (0.831) to beat the neutral (0.852), are the theory's optimum, not a defect of majority voting. The neutral is a dictator by structural cancellation (Estlund's opinion-leader case without deference): two near-constant opposed voters (p_w + p_c = 1.033, exactly one is right on almost every item) sum to a constant and leave the third seat as the tiebreak on every item. (2) Correlated votes: Ladha 1992 shows negatively correlated votes raise majority accuracy, and on the verdict layer our advocates' errors are almost perfectly negatively correlated; yet the pair contributes nothing because Ladha's benefit requires each voter's competence above 1/2 and non-degenerate variance, and a pair that always splits is a constant. The measured phi = -0.72 anti-correlation lives in the objection layer, which is not a vote on the proposition, so no jury theorem can harvest it as votes; it can only be used as the error flag we built (4.56x error density; +0.193 with an external judge on the flagged 20%). This objection-vs-verdict dissociation is a List-Pettit/doctrinal-paradox shape: aggregating reasons and aggregating conclusions come apart. (3) Iteration cannot converge to truth: DeGroot 1974 gives the fixed point as pi . x(0), a re-weighting of round-0 opinions with no new evidence; Friedkin-Johnsen 1990 and Acemoglu et al. 2013 show that with opposed stubborn agents (our role-locked advocates, unmoved across 7 rounds and still at 0.946 role-lock with the stake removed) there is no consensus at all, only an equilibrium pinned to the stubborn opinions, which pull the neutral symmetrically toward a constant. Hence the measured +0.012 [-0.039, +0.063] from feeding dissent back. Lorenz et al. 2011 is the human replication of that null and Becker et al. 2017 names our functional topology: a complete graph whose only informative node is the centre is their centralized case, where influence increases error (neutral 0.912 alone vs 0.852 in the panel). (4) Golub-Jackson 2010: the 'no agent too influential' condition is violated maximally (pi_max = 1), but the deeper failure is the precondition that each agent carries an independent noisy signal; embodiment replaces signal with role, so diluting the neutral's influence would lower accuracy. (5) Why the external override works and internal correction does not: Dietrich-Spiekermann 2013 make independence a property of the causal network; every seat and every self-sample shares the common cause 'this model's posterior on this item', so the self-consistency sensor is weaker than the embodied flag (+0.020) and feedback is null, while a cross-vendor judge has a different common cause and adds +0.193. Prelec et al. 2017 solve the same shared-bias problem with a meta-prediction layer the panel cannot supply; Schoenegger et al. 2024 show the LLM analogue (exposure to an external median improves an LLM 17-28%, and plain averaging beats exposure). (6) Diversity: Hong-Page 2004 predicts a diverse panel beats a high-ability one; our mixed-role panel is worse than homogeneous (-0.026 [-0.047, -0.007]), consistent with Thompson 2014's critique and with Bahrami et al. 2010's finding that communicating with much weaker partners makes two heads worse than the better one; Zollman 2010 classifies role-locked diversity as the permanent kind that prevents convergence. Navajas et al. 2018 found small-group debate beats large crowds with humans who can update; our agents cannot, and the result reverses. Net: the literature already predicts embodiment as a near-total individual control (Mercier-Sperber: proactive case-making produces confirmation bias; evaluation stays informative), predicts that the resulting community is a jury of one, and predicts that iterating the same protocol cannot add evidence. What our results add that none of these test is the positive part: a same-source embodied panel is a good error sensor even though it is a poor generator, and objectivity is obtained by routing the panel's self-flag to a causally independent external node rather than by any wiring of the panel itself. That is a decorrelation-by-external-node theory of objectivity, not a graph-structure-does-the-reconciling theory; the graph's contribution is confined to producing the flag.

closeness_disputes.why: It is the only other published multi-model debate on the same task (AITA blame assignment, 1,000 Reddit dilemmas, 30,000+ debates) and its independent variable is exactly thesis (B)'s variable: the interaction structure of the collective, with measured conformity and inertia effects. That it does not score against the crowd verdict is the gap the programme fills, which makes it the paper the related-work section must be positioned against, not a 3 buried mid-list.

It is a formal framework evaluated on four QA benchmarks with no interest assignment, no per-seat information accounting, no dissent-as-flag, and no external judge; its one point of contact is the 'same-model debate converges to the majority' mechanism. That same mechanism is now stated more directly for the programme's purposes by Choi, Zhu and Li (NeurIPS 2025, verified below), who decompose MAD into majority voting plus debate, show voting accounts for the gain and prove a martingale over beliefs, which maps one-to-one onto 'effective voter count is one' and 'a re-sample of the same posterior'. Estornell belongs at 3 alongside Zhu 2026 as the formal backing for the steering null.

It is the only entry in the list that assigns an adversarial INTEREST (sneaky prover) rather than a truth-indexed position, with the verifier as the locus of truth. That is structurally the closest analogue to a stake-driven advocate plus external judge, which is the programme's headline shape. The training-time versus prompt-time difference is real but is a difference in how the interest is instilled, not in the design. Rating it below ChatEval-adjacent work understates its relevance to thesis (A).

closeness_disputes.why: It measures the role-lock quantity, which is the sweep's reason for a 4, and it is still the closest work on (A). But on inspection of the HTML it has none of the ingredients of (B): the three advocates score independently (no rounds, no message passing, no graph), the 'supervisor' is a rule-based weighted sum rather than an aggregating LLM, and the roles are filled by DIFFERENT vendor models (charitable = Claude Sonnet 4.6 or Mistral Large, critical = Gemini 2.5 Flash), so 'role vs prior' is confounded with 'model'. No ground-truth verdict accuracy, no sycophancy. That is three of the four things the programme measured absent; 3 is the honest number.

The programme's headline shape is: assigned opposed advocates whose own verdicts are uninformative, a majority that collapses to one seat, internal feedback that nets nothing, and objectivity recovered only by an external decorrelated judge reading the disagreement. Khan et al. is the only entry that builds exactly that allocation of labour on ground-truth items and reports judge accuracy against it (48->76 LLM, 60->88 human). It is closer to the measured result than any persona-cost paper the sweep rated 3, and closer to the shape of the finding than Dietrich.

closeness_disputes.why: Its experimental design is the same as li2024sparse (rated 3): sparsity as the manipulated variable, benchmark accuracy as the dependent variable, fully-connected graph as the comparator. What it adds is a causal-analysis lens and a learned topology (EIB-Learner). It has no truth-tracking dependent variable beyond benchmark accuracy, no order parameter, no effective-voter-count, and no comparison against the collective's best member or a single call, which are the three things the strand question asks for. han2026conformity earned its 4 by putting a truth-tracking task on the y-axis with a tunable self/social weight; Shen has neither. The 'graph's job is to suppress bad-node propagation' reading is an interpretation of the same sparse-beats-dense result, not a separate measurement.

The programme's own just-run ablation changes what counts as its control input: role-lock stays at 0.946 with only the directional case-making assignment and no stake. Liang et al.'s affirmative/negative 'tit-for-tat' debaters are exactly that directional assignment, wired to a judge node, i.e. the programme's topology minus the neutral seat. It is the only entry in the strand that instantiates the programme's node roles, and its observations that (i) the judge does the work and (ii) the judge is biased toward its own model family are the two halves of the programme's 'objectivity came from an external decorrelated node' result. It does not vary topology or compute N_eff, so it is not a 5, but it is closer than the 3-rated single-call-vs-discussion comparisons.

important_work_the_sweep_missed: VERIFIED. Golub, Benjamin and Matthew O. Jackson (2010). 'Naive Learning in Social Networks and the Wisdom of Crowds.' American Economic Journal: Microeconomics 2(1):112-149, DOI 10.1257/mic.2.1.112. Fetched https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/mic.2.1.112 (title, authors, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI confirmed). This is the canonical 'graph theory of objectivity' the PI's thesis (B) is describing: agents holding independent noisy signals and repeatedly averaging neighbours' opinions on a network converge to the truth if and only if the influence of the most influential agent vanishes as the society grows. The programme's finding that the 3-seat majority equals the neutral seat on 1,663/1,663 debates is a maximal-influence node in this sense, so Golub-Jackson predicts no wisdom of crowds for that graph. The strand has no social-choice or network-learning theory at all; this is the biggest gap.

closeness_disputes.why: A four-page 1974 note with no ground truth, no accuracy notion, no roles and no stubborn agents. Its only use here is the fixed-point pi.x(0) argument, and that argument is made more precisely for the programme's actual case (two opposed non-updating agents) by Friedkin-Johnsen 1990 and Acemoglu et al. 2013, both rated 3. Rating DeGroot equal to them overstates it; 2 is consistent with Boland and List-Pettit.

This is the theory paper whose model is literally the three-seat panel: agents who never update (the role-locked advocates), holding different fixed opinions, plus regular agents (the neutral) who average; result is no consensus, persistent disagreement, expectation pinned to a weighted average of the stubborn opinions. It predicts both the role-lock persistence across 7 rounds and the iteration null more directly than Golub-Jackson, whose precondition the panel violates. It should sit at 4 alongside Golub-Jackson and Bahrami.

It is the only entry that predicts the exact production/evaluation split the programme measured: an agent told to make a case shows confirmation bias in what it produces (verdicts carry no item information; the stake-removal ablation shows the case-making assignment alone does it), while its evaluation of the other side stays informative (objections are a 4.56x error-density signal). No other entry explains why the collective is a sensor but not a generator. That is closer to the finding's shape than most of the 3-rated formal results.

It is the human experiment with the same protocol shape as the programme (small groups debate to a consensus, consensus is scored against ground truth, compared with independent individuals), with N=5,180, and the programme's headline result is its reversal (debate 0.843 loses to single call 0.912). A direct human precedent whose result the programme inverts under role assignment deserves the same rating as Bahrami 2010.

The programme's most novel structural finding is that aggregating at the objection (reasons) level yields a usable signal while aggregating at the verdict (conclusions) level yields nothing beyond the neutral seat. List-Pettit is the canonical formal statement that premise-level and conclusion-level aggregation come apart, and the paper will need it to name that dissociation. It is closer to the finding than Boland or Estlund, which are also at 2.

verified_entries.title: Rule 804. Hearsay Exceptions; Declarant Unavailable -- (b)(3) Statement Against Interest
verified_entries.what_it_shows: The rule admits, as an exception to hearsay, a statement that a reasonable person in the declarant's position would have made only if believing it true because it was so contrary to the declarant's proprietary or pecuniary interest, invalidated a claim, or exposed the declarant to civil or criminal liability, and (in criminal cases) requires corroborating circumstances; the Advisory Committee note states the rationale as the assumption that persons do not make statements damaging to themselves unless satisfied for good reason that they are true.
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The evidentiary form of the credible-signal principle (design document section 3): the paper's flag treats an advocate's objection to a verdict that favours its own side as informative for the same reason the law treats a declaration against interest as trustworthy, the speaker had every incentive not to make it. Cite where the principle is introduced, alongside milgrom1986relying and lipman1995robust, and note that the paper's advocates have an assigned interest that the reader knows with certainty, so the inference the rule licenses is immediate rather than reconstructed from the declarant's position.

verified_entries.title: Declarations against Interest: An Exception to the Hearsay Rule
verified_entries.fetch_method_2026_09_14: Browser pane (WebFetch returned JSTOR client-challenge shell)
verified_entries.what_it_shows: A 69-page law-review treatment of the declaration-against-interest exception to the hearsay rule; law reviews carry no abstract, and the first-page preview read on JSTOR opens by characterising the development of the hearsay exceptions as haphazard and proceeds to examine the requirements of this one (the secondary literature found in search describes it as the standard critical treatment, more thorough than Wigmore's, but that characterisation was not verified from the article itself).
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The doctrinal source behind the evidentiary intuition the design document names in section 3; pair with fre804b3 when the paper says an admission against interest is credible, so that the legal analogy rests on a treatise-level treatment rather than on the rule text alone. Use only for the general proposition; do not attribute specific holdings to it without reading the body.

verified_entries.title: Persuasion by Cheap Talk
verified_entries.what_it_shows: In multidimensional cheap talk from an expert to a decision maker, an expert with state-independent preferences can always make credible comparative statements that trade off the expert's incentive to exaggerate on each dimension; such talk benefits the expert when her preferences are quasiconvex, and competition among decision makers can eliminate the decision maker's gain.
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The paper's advocates have state-independent preferences over the verdict (their opening verdict is a constant of the role, lock 0.971), which is exactly Chakraborty and Harbaugh's sender. Their result says what such a sender can still credibly say: a statement that costs it on some dimension. The against-interest objection is the one-dimensional case, and their multidimensional result is the theory for section 3's hypothesis that ESH and NAH verdicts undermine each advocate on one of two stake dimensions (own party's innocence, other party's fault), so that comparative objections become the credible messages there and the loser set must be computed over stake dimensions; cite with battaglini2002multiple and krishna2001model in the cheap-talk cluster.

verified_entries.title: Naive, Biased, yet Bayesian: Can Juries Interpret Selectively Produced Evidence?
verified_entries.what_it_shows: In a model of civil litigation where interested parties incur costs to produce statistical evidence and present a selected subset to a jury that is naive (treats the evidence as a random sample) and biased by prior beliefs, the full-information decision is nevertheless reached as long as both litigants choose to produce evidence, so criticisms of juries based on bias or heuristic rules may be overstated.
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The law-and-economics counterpart of the paper's naive uninterested moderator (design document 2(b)): a decider that reads the advocates' output at face value still reaches the right answer when both sides produce, because competition in production does the correcting. It predicts the paper's finding that the moderator need not be sophisticated for the verdict layer, and its condition, that both litigants produce, is the paper's silence case in reverse, since on Scruples Dilemmas the favoured advocate has nothing to produce against the verdict and the sensor is silent. Cite with milgrom1986relying and shin1998adversarial in the adversarial-procedure cluster.

verified_entries.title: Relying on the Information of Interested—and Potentially Dishonest—Parties
verified_entries.what_it_shows: Models evidence production under judicial or administrative oversight when the regulated party may fabricate, with the agent's fine depending on evidence whose production cost depends on how the agent actually behaved; finds that factual accuracy has no inherent connection to deterrence, that perfectly reliable evidence can be suboptimal, and that penalties above the socially optimal level can be efficient.
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The boundary of the credible-signal principle when the against-interest party can lie cheaply. Milgrom and Roberts' reliance on interested parties (which the paper's title of section 2(a) rests on) assumes claims are verifiable; Sanchirico's title answers theirs and shows what changes when fabrication is possible. The paper's advocates argue over a fixed shared account and may not invent facts, which is the partial provability of lipman1995robust, and the nano model, whose advocates object regardless of stake and flood the sensor, is the machine instance of a party whose statements against interest carry no cost. Cite where the paper states the no-invented-facts condition and where it reports nano's flooding.

verified_entries.title: A Theory of Credibility
verified_entries.fetch_method_2026_09_14: Browser pane (WebFetch returned JSTOR client-challenge shell; OUP restud page rendered navigation only)
verified_entries.what_it_shows: Presents models in which one agent must decide whether to trust another whose motives are uncertain; reliability can only be communicated through actions, so it pays to build a reputation by consistently providing accurate information, the theory justifies long-term arrangements without binding contracts and describes when an agent cashes in a reputation.
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The contrast case for the paper's control. Sobel's receiver does not know the sender's interest and must infer credibility from a history of behaviour; the paper assigns the interest by brief and verifies that the copy takes it (99.7 and 97.4 percent of opening statements), so the receiver knows the sender's interest before the first message and a single statement against it is credible with no reputation to build. Cite in the credible-signal section to say why assignment, not learning, is what makes the one-shot objection informative, and why the sensor needs role-lock (soft lock on haiku is a sender of uncertain motive, and the sensor weakens there).

verified_entries.title: Formal systems for persuasion dialogue
verified_entries.what_it_shows: Reviews formal systems that regulate persuasion dialogues in which two or more participants try to resolve a difference of opinion by persuading each other; taking a game-theoretic view, it proposes a formal specification of the main elements of a persuasion dialogue system (participants, moves, protocol, commitments, burden of proof and outcome rules) and uses it to review the main systems, focusing on regulating the interaction between agents rather than on individual agent design.
verified_entries.relation_to_paper: The computational-argumentation frame for the paper's protocol. The seven-step sequence (open, rebut, restate, verdict, accept or object, integrate, vote) is a persuasion dialogue system in Prakken's sense, and his separation of the protocol from the agents' strategies is the paper's separation of the graph from the model: the paper holds the protocol fixed and varies who is set against whom and who decides. His burden-of-proof element is the formal home of the paper's loser set L(v), the seat on which a one-loser verdict places the burden to object; cite where the graph is defined and where the flag is stated as a rule over who objects, as the pointer into the dialogue-games and burden-of-proof literature that Dung-style frameworks (not verified here, see not_verified) formalise.
